en: to aid; to help; to assist

examples.en: My friends joined in on the cleaning too.
The wind joined in, so it felt even colder.

examples.ko: 우리 팀을 응원하는 사람들이 점점 가세해요.
examples.en: More and more people are joining in to cheer for our team.
My father will lend a hand with this too.

examples.ko: 비까지 가세한 날이라 길이 많이 막혔어요.
examples.en: With rain on top of everything, the roads were badly jammed.

examples.ko: 이웃 사람들이 가세하자 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
examples.en: Once the neighbors pitched in, the work finished quickly.

explain: '돕다'는 어떤 상황에서든 쓰지만 '가세하다'는 이미 진행 중인 일이나 싸움에 힘을 보태러 끼어드는 느낌이에요. '~에 가세하다'로 쓰고, '악재가 가세하다'처럼 나쁜 일이 겹칠 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I helped Mom with the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가세하다'와 비슷하지만 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 가세하다 but an easy everyday word.

phrases.example: 모두 힘을 보태서 일이 빨리 끝났어요.
phrases.en: Everyone chipped in, so the work finished quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 도와서 힘이 더해질 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural phrase for adding one's strength to a task.

phrases.en: With rain joining in, the road got even more jammed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일이 겹칠 때도 연결형으로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The connecting form can also be used when bad things pile up.

explain_en: Unlike the all-purpose 돕다, 가세하다 means stepping into something already under way to add your weight to it. It takes 에 ('~에 가세하다'), and bad factors can also 'join in', as in '악재가 가세하다'.

en: staying power; stamina at the finish

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 뒷심이 강해서 후반에 역전했어요.
examples.en: Our team has strong staying power, so it turned the game around in the second half.

examples.ko: 마라톤은 뒷심이 부족하면 끝까지 달리기 어려워요.
examples.en: In a marathon, it's hard to run to the end without staying power.
We did well early on, but ran out of steam and lost.
I showed my finishing strength at the end and took first place.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 뒷심이 약해서 결말이 아쉬워요.
examples.en: That drama lacks staying power, so the ending is disappointing.
Studying is about finishing strong, so keep going until the end.

explain: 일이나 경기의 끝 무렵까지 버티거나 마지막에 내는 힘을 말해요. '뒷심이 있다/강하다/부족하다/달리다/발휘하다'처럼 써요. 뒤에서 도와주는 힘이라는 뜻도 있지만, 일상에서는 앞의 뜻으로 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We ran out of steam in the second half and lost the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝 무렵에 힘이 모자란다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means running out of strength near the end.

phrases.en: We showed our staying power at the end and won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝에서 힘을 내어 해낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means summoning strength at the finish to pull it off.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 뒷심이 있어서 끝까지 믿을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: That player has stamina at the finish, so you can trust them to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝까지 힘을 잃지 않는 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone who keeps their strength until the end.

explain_en: It means the strength to hold out until the end of a task or game, or the force you show at the finish. It is used as '뒷심이 있다/강하다/부족하다/달리다/발휘하다'. It can also mean support from behind, but in daily life the first meaning is used more often.

examples.en: He worked constantly and achieved his dream.
Language changes continuously with the times.
If you practice constantly, your pronunciation will get better too.

examples.ko: 회사는 부단히 새로운 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The company is constantly looking for new methods.
The teacher kept showing interest in the students without letting up.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 부단히 도전한 끝에 우승했어요.
examples.en: That team won the championship after challenging itself nonstop.

explain: '끊임없이', '꾸준히'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있는 느낌이라 글, 연설, 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 가장 흔한 짝은 '부단히 노력하다'예요. 말할 때는 '계속', '꾸준히'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The players keep striving to win the championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이고 격식 있는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, often seen in formal writing and news.

phrases.en: Technology is changing continuously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끊이지 않고 계속 바뀐다는 뜻으로 글에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in writing to mean changing without stopping.

phrases.en: He studied without stopping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 말할 때도 자연스럽게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and natural to use in speech too.

explain_en: It is close to '끊임없이' and '꾸준히' but sounds more formal, so it appears often in writing, speeches and the news. The most common pairing is '부단히 노력하다'. In casual speech, '계속' or '꾸준히' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The two of them pledged to stay together for life.

examples.ko: 신입 사원들이 서약을 하고 일을 시작했어요.
examples.en: The new employees took a pledge and began work.
I wrote my name on the pledge form and stamped it.

examples.ko: 학생들은 정직하게 시험을 보겠다는 서약을 했어요.
examples.en: The students made a pledge to take the exam honestly.
That pledge was not broken easily.
At the wedding, the bride and groom read their vows.

explain: '약속'은 일상에서 가볍게 쓰지만 '서약'은 맹세처럼 무겁고 공식적인 약속이에요. 보통 '서약을 하다'라고 하고, 문서로 쓰면 '서약서'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: We pledged to keep the secret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '서약'을 동사로 바꾼 말이고 '-겠다고'와 잘 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 서약, often used with -겠다고.

phrases.en: I wrote my name and signed the pledge document.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문서로 된 서약은 '서약서'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A written pledge is called 서약서.

phrases.en: He kept his wedding vow to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번 한 서약을 어기지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone does not break a pledge once made.

explain_en: 약속 is a light, everyday promise, but 서약 is a heavy, formal promise close to an oath. You usually say '서약을 하다', and the written form is called 서약서.

examples.ko: 외래어를 우리말로 바꾸는 순화 작업이 진행 중이에요.
examples.en: Work to replace loanwords with Korean words is under way.

examples.ko: 거친 표현의 순화가 필요하다는 의견이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people think rough expressions need to be toned down.
Students also took part in the campaign to purify the language.

examples.ko: 방송에서 쓰는 말의 순화는 중요한 문제예요.
examples.en: Refining the language used on broadcasts is an important issue.
I gathered and organized the words to be replaced.
A campaign to clean up swearing was held at school.

explain: 우리말에서는 주로 '국어 순화', '언어 순화'처럼 거칠거나 어려운 말, 외래어를 고운 말이나 쉬운 우리말로 다듬는 일에 써요. 이렇게 바꾼 말은 '순화어'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 국어 순화를 위해 어려운 외래어를 바꿔요.
phrases.en: They replace difficult foreign words in order to refine Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리말을 고운 말, 쉬운 말로 다듬는 일을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to refining Korean into gentler, easier words.

phrases.en: The school held language-refinement education.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특히 거친 말을 고운 말로 바꾸자는 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often means replacing rough speech with kinder speech.

phrases.en: 'Doumi' is a refined word that replaced a foreign word.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순화해서 새로 만든 우리말을 부르는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for the new Korean word created by refinement.

explain_en: In Korean it is mostly used for language, as in '국어 순화' or '언어 순화': refining rough or difficult words and loanwords into gentler or easier Korean. The replacement words are called '순화어'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 매일 아침 재료를 엄선해서 요리해요.
examples.en: This restaurant carefully selects its ingredients every morning to cook.
The judges carefully selected the nominees.

examples.ko: 엄선한 과일만 골라서 선물 세트를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a gift set with only carefully selected fruit.

examples.ko: 좋은 책만 엄선하는 작은 도서관이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small library that only picks carefully chosen good books.
The boss personally chose the business partners with great care.

examples.ko: 수많은 지원자 중에서 세 명을 엄선할 거예요.
examples.en: We will carefully select three people from the many applicants.

explain: '고르다'보다 훨씬 신중하게 가려 뽑는 느낌이고 격식 있는 말이에요. 광고나 상품 설명에서 '엄선한 재료'처럼 많이 보여요.

phrases.example: 엄선한 재료로 만든 빵이라 맛이 좋아요.
phrases.en: The bread is made with carefully selected ingredients, so it tastes good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고나 상품 설명에서 많이 보이는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing in ads and product descriptions.

phrases.en: Only carefully chosen works are hung at the exhibition.
phrases.nuance_ko: '엄선되다'는 가려 뽑힌 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 엄선되다 describes something that has been carefully chosen.

phrases.en: The owner tasted them personally and selected them carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: '직접'을 붙이면 믿을 만하다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 직접 gives a feeling of trustworthiness.

explain_en: It feels much more careful and formal than '고르다' (to pick). You often see it in ads and product descriptions, as in '엄선한 재료' (carefully selected ingredients).

examples.en: This machine filters the dust out of the water.
If you strain the broth through a cloth, it becomes clear.
I bought a mask that filters the air.
The filter is purifying the rainwater.
I drink the coffee after filtering it.
It's a vacuum cleaner that can filter out dust.

explain: 기계나 실험, 정수 이야기에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이고, 일상에서는 '거르다'를 많이 써요. 정보나 말에도 '여과해서 듣다'처럼 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Please sift the powder finely with a sieve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '여과하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word used instead of 여과하다.

phrases.example: 인터넷 정보는 여과해서 받아들이는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's better to filter information from the internet before accepting it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들은 말이나 정보를 그대로 믿지 않고 가려서 받아들인다는 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use meaning not believing information as is, but sorting it out first.

phrases.example: 정수기에는 물을 깨끗하게 하는 여과 장치가 있어요.
phrases.en: A water purifier has a filter device that cleans the water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 공기를 걸러 주는 기계 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the machine part that filters water or air.

explain_en: It is a formal word used for machines, experiments and water purification, while everyday speech prefers '거르다'. It can also be used figuratively for information or words, as in '여과해서 듣다'.

examples.ko: 그는 자진 신고를 해서 벌이 줄었어요.
examples.en: He turned himself in voluntarily, so his penalty was reduced.
He announced his intention to resign of his own accord.
The voluntary payment period lasts until next week.
I took on the cleaning of my own accord.
No one stepped forward voluntarily.

examples.ko: 이 일은 자진 참여하는 사람만 하면 돼요.
examples.en: Only people who join voluntarily need to do this.

explain: '자진 신고', '자진 퇴사', '자진 납부'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 시키지 않아도 스스로 한다는 뜻을 더해요. 일상에서 '자원하다'나 '스스로'도 비슷하게 쓰지만, '자진'은 신고, 퇴사, 납부 같은 공식적인 일에 특히 많이 어울려요.

phrases.en: If you pay taxes voluntarily, there are benefits.
phrases.nuance_ko: 독촉받기 전에 스스로 돈을 낸다는 뜻이고, 공식적인 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paying on one's own before being pressed; used in official contexts.

phrases.en: The CEO took responsibility and resigned of their own accord.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 시키지 않았는데 스스로 물러난다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Stepping down without being forced; common in news.

phrases.en: The suspect voluntarily appeared at the police station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부르지 않았는데 스스로 찾아가 나타나는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Showing up on one's own without being summoned.

explain_en: It often attaches before another word, as in 자진 신고, 자진 퇴사, and 자진 납부, to show something was done without being told. 스스로 is similar in daily speech, but 자진 fits especially well with formal matters like reporting, resigning, or paying.

examples.en: How did you come up with the name for your new cafe?
I named my new puppy 'Tofu'.

examples.ko: 새 가게를 멋지게 작명해 줄 사람을 찾아요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to give my new shop a great name.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 별명을 재미있게 작명해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend gave me a funny nickname.

examples.ko: 작명하기 전에 이름의 뜻을 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to check the meaning of a name before you choose it.

examples.ko: 신제품을 작명하느라 회의를 세 번이나 했어요.
examples.en: We had three meetings just to name the new product.

explain: 일상에서는 '이름을 짓다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '작명하다'는 조금 딱딱하거나, 가게·제품·별명처럼 이름을 붙이는 일을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: What should we name the cat?
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '작명하다'보다 훨씬 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural than '작명하다' in daily speech.

phrases.example: 우리 새 가게를 멋지게 작명해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please give our new shop a great name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가에게 이름을 지어 달라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone to come up with a name.

phrases.en: My friend gave me a great nickname.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름을 잘 붙였다는 칭찬을 부사와 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with an adverb to praise a well-chosen name.

explain_en: In daily life '이름을 짓다' sounds much more natural. '작명하다' is a bit formal and is used for giving names to shops, products or nicknames.

examples.en: After the war, the rebuilding of the city began.
Rebuilding takes a lot of time and money.
The villagers helped with the school's reconstruction.

examples.ko: 화재로 불탄 시장의 재건 공사가 끝났어요.
examples.en: The reconstruction work on the market that burned down in the fire is finished.

examples.ko: 나라의 재건을 위해 많은 사람이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people gathered to rebuild the country.
Rebuilding is not an easy job.

explain: 집이나 다리 같은 건물뿐 아니라 나라, 경제, 삶이 무너졌다가 다시 일어서는 일에도 써요. '재건 공사', '재건을 돕다'처럼 말해요. 건물 하나를 고치는 일에는 '수리'나 '복구'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 다리의 재건 공사가 한 달 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: The reconstruction work on the bridge took a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무너진 건물이나 시설을 다시 짓는 공사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Construction work to build a collapsed building or facility again.

phrases.en: Many countries helped with the rebuilding of the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려움을 겪은 곳이 다시 일어서도록 도와줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when helping a place that suffered hardship to get back on its feet.

phrases.example: 전쟁 뒤에 나라는 경제 재건에 힘썼어요.
phrases.en: After the war, the country worked hard on economic reconstruction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이 아니라 나라의 경제를 다시 일으키는 일에도 쓴다는 것을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows that the word applies not only to buildings but also to rebuilding a country's economy.

explain_en: It covers not only buildings and bridges but also a country, an economy or a life being built up again. Say '재건 공사' or '재건을 돕다'. For fixing a single building, '수리' or '복구' is more common.

en: to break through (a deadlock or crisis)

examples.ko: 매출이 줄어서 회사가 위기를 타개할 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: Sales have dropped, so the company is looking for a way to break out of the crisis.

examples.ko: 이 난관을 타개하려면 모두의 도움이 필요해요.
examples.en: To get through this difficulty, we need everyone's help.
It is hard to break through this situation alone.
We overcame the crisis with a new idea.

examples.ko: 불황을 타개하는 데 거의 일 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took almost a year to get out of the slump.

examples.ko: 이 침체를 타개해 보려고 모두 모여 회의했어요.
examples.en: We all got together for a meeting to try to break out of this stagnation.

explain: '극복하다'와 비슷하지만 막혀 있는 상황을 뚫고 나갈 길을 찾는다는 느낌이 있어요. 목적어는 주로 위기, 난관, 불황 같은 어려운 상황이고 '타개책'이라는 말도 같이 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The government announced a breakthrough plan to get through the recession.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 상황을 뚫고 나갈 방법을 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for a way to break through a difficult situation.

phrases.example: 가게 주인은 새 메뉴로 불황을 타개하려고 해요.
phrases.en: The shop owner is trying to break through the slump with a new menu.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불황' 같은 큰 어려움에 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation that suits big hardships like a recession.

phrases.en: He overcame hardship and achieved his dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타개하다'보다 뜻이 넓고 일상에서도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader in meaning than 타개하다 and used often in daily life.

explain_en: It is similar to '극복하다' (to overcome) but carries the feel of finding a way through a blocked situation. The object is usually a crisis, difficulty or slump, and the related word '타개책' (a way out) is also common.

en: to molt; to shed the skin; to slough

examples.en: Snakes molt several times as they grow.
I want to break away from old habits.

examples.ko: 매미는 나무 위에서 탈피한 뒤에 날아요.
examples.en: Cicadas fly after molting on a tree.

examples.ko: 옛날 방식에서 탈피해서 새 앱을 만들었어요.
examples.en: We broke away from the old way and made a new app.
A crab grows bigger each time it molts.
Without breaking away from the mold, there is no progress.

explain: 곤충, 뱀 같은 동물이 껍질을 벗을 때도 쓰고, 사람이 낡은 생각이나 방식을 버릴 때도 써요. 사람 이야기에서는 '~에서 탈피하다'로 쓰고 '벗어나다'보다 조금 딱딱해요.

phrases.en: Snakes shed their skin as they grow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탈피하다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 말이라 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way to say 탈피하다, more natural in everyday talk.

phrases.en: You need to break away from stereotypes for new ideas to appear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 방식을 바꿀 때 '~에서 탈피하다'로 쓰고, '벗어나다'보다 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as '~에서 탈피하다' for changing a way of thinking; it is stiffer than 벗어나다.

phrases.en: If you can't break away from the old way, you fall behind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형 '-지 못하다'를 붙여 벗어나지 못하는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form '-지 못하다' describes being unable to break away.

explain_en: It is used when animals such as insects and snakes shed their skin, and also when a person gives up old thinking or ways. For people it is '~에서 탈피하다', which sounds a bit stiffer than '벗어나다'.

en: determination to win; certainty of victory

examples.en: I'll present our team's winning strategy.
The players entered the stadium determined to win.

examples.ko: 경기 전에 모두 필승! 하고 외쳤어요.
examples.en: Before the game, everyone shouted 'Victory!'
Their will to win this match is tremendous.
We are saving our trump card.
The players, vowing to win, had bright expressions.

explain: '반드시 이긴다'는 뜻으로 '필승 전략', '필승 각오', '필승 의지', '필승 카드'처럼 다른 말 앞에서 많이 써요. 응원 구호로 '필승!'이라고 외치기도 해요. 반대로 '반드시 진다'는 말은 '필패'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The players steeled their resolve to win.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반드시 이기겠다는 마음가짐을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a mindset of being determined to win.

phrases.en: The coach pulled out his last winning card.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이기기 위해 꼭 쓰는 방법이나 선수를 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to refer to a method or player used to secure victory.

phrases.example: 감독이 이번 경기를 위한 필승 전략을 짰어요.
phrases.en: The coach came up with a winning strategy for this game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반드시 이기기 위해 세운 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a plan made to be sure of winning.

explain_en: It carries the sense of 'certain to win' and is often placed before other nouns, as in 필승 전략, 필승 각오, 필승 의지 and 필승 카드. People also shout '필승!' as a cheer. The opposite, 'certain to lose', is '필패'.

examples.en: The president arrived under police escort.

examples.ko: 배는 군함의 호위 속에 항구를 떠났어요.
examples.en: The ship left port under the escort of a warship.

examples.ko: 왕을 호위하는 병사가 문 앞에 서 있어요.
examples.en: The soldiers guarding the king stand at the door.
Escort vehicles follow in front and behind.
In the movie, the bodyguard warrior protected the hero.
Without an escort, this road is dangerous.

explain: 호위는 중요한 사람이나 물건을 따라다니며 지키는 일이에요. 경호는 주로 사람을 지키는 일에 쓰고, 호위는 함께 움직이며 둘러싸 지키는 모습에 더 잘 어울려요. 옛날 이야기와 군대, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 왕은 병사들의 호위를 받으며 성을 나갔어요.
phrases.en: The king left the castle escorted by soldiers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지켜 주는 사람들과 함께 움직이는 사람 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the point of view of the person being escorted and moving along with the guards.

phrases.en: The guard is standing at the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 사람을 따라다니며 지키는 군인을 말해요. 옛날 이야기나 역사에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soldier who accompanies and protects an important person; common in old tales and history.

phrases.example: 대통령 차 앞뒤로 호위 차량이 따라가요.
phrases.en: Escort vehicles follow in front of and behind the president's car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 사람의 차를 둘러싸고 함께 달리는 차를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Cars that drive alongside and around an important person's car.

explain_en: 호위 means accompanying an important person or thing in order to protect it. 경호 is more about guarding a person; 호위 fits protection while moving together. It shows up in historical stories, the military and the news.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 홀연히 떠났어요.
examples.en: He left suddenly without a word.
All of a sudden the fog lifted and the mountain came into view.

examples.ko: 어느 날 홀연히 나타난 낯선 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a stranger who appeared out of nowhere one day.

examples.ko: 친구는 회사를 그만두고 홀연히 여행을 갔어요.
examples.en: My friend quit the company and suddenly went off traveling.

examples.ko: 홀연히 옛 생각이 나서 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: Old memories suddenly came back to me and I teared up.
The magician vanished from the stage in an instant.

explain: 이야기나 글 같은 느낌이 있어서 '사라지다', '나타나다', '떠나다'와 자주 함께 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '갑자기'나 '불쑥'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The cat suddenly vanished.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예고 없이 어느새 없어졌다는 이야기 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a storybook feel of vanishing without warning.

phrases.example: 어둠 속에서 한 사람이 홀연히 나타났어요.
phrases.en: A person suddenly appeared out of the darkness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디서 왔는지 모르게 갑자기 모습을 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone shows up suddenly with no sign of where they came from.

phrases.en: Suddenly, it started pouring rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 홀연히보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 홀연히 and the most natural choice in daily conversation.

explain_en: It has a storytelling or literary feel and often appears with '사라지다', '나타나다' and '떠나다'. In daily conversation '갑자기' or '불쑥' sounds more natural.

en: to grab; to seize; to grip

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 말 한마디로 반 아이들을 휘어잡아요.
examples.en: That teacher gets the whole class under control with a single word.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 첫날부터 회의 분위기를 휘어잡았어요.
examples.en: The new employee took command of the meeting's mood from day one.

examples.ko: 가수가 노래 몇 소절로 관객을 휘어잡았어요.
examples.en: The singer captivated the audience with just a few bars.

examples.ko: 팀장이 되려면 사람들을 휘어잡는 힘이 필요해요.
examples.en: To become a team leader, you need the strength to take charge of people.
I grabbed the shaky railing tight and barely climbed up.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 눈빛 하나로 무대를 휘어잡을 수 있어요.
examples.en: That actor can command the stage with just a look.

explain: 물건을 꽉 붙잡는 뜻도 있지만, 사람이나 분위기를 완전히 자기 쪽으로 끌어와 장악한다는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. 카리스마가 있는 사람이나 무대, 회의 분위기와 잘 어울려요. 단순히 '잡다'라고 하면 이런 장악하는 느낌이 안 나요.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 첫 노래부터 공연장 분위기를 휘어잡았어요.
phrases.en: From the first song, that singer took control of the concert hall's atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이나 공연의 분위기를 자기 쪽으로 끌어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone pulls the mood of a gathering or show their way.
phrases.en_equiv: to take control of the mood

phrases.en: The actor's performance gripped the audience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 눈을 못 떼게 완전히 집중시킨다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests holding people so completely that they can't look away.

phrases.example: 새 팀장이 팀 분위기를 빠르게 장악했어요.
phrases.en: The new team leader quickly took control of the team atmosphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이에요. 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but more formal, common in writing and news.

explain_en: It can mean gripping something tightly, but it is used more often for taking full control of people or an atmosphere. It fits charismatic people, stages and meeting moods. Plain '잡다' wouldn't carry that sense of commanding the scene.
